Look in the order_payments table — the column payment_installments records the number of installments used for a given payment on an order.

Notes and how to use it (conceptual, no SQL):
- order_payments rows are linked to orders by order_id.
- A single order can have multiple rows (payment_sequential) if multiple payment methods were used; each row has its own payment_installments and payment_value.
- To get the installments for an order, examine all order_payments rows for that order (e.g., the most common approach is to use the payment_installments from the primary payment row or aggregate/count distinct values across rows depending on your definition).
- You can also combine payment_installments with payment_type and payment_value to analyze installment patterns by payment method or by amount.
- To focus on 1–5 installments, filter payment_installments between 1 and 5 in your analysis.

(See order_payments in the schema documentation for column names and relationships.)
